newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian gold slips on profit-taking, silver rises.
newsitem.headline: Indian gold slips on profit-taking, silver rises.

text.p: ** Gold 24 carat closes five rupees higher at 4,830 rupees per 10 gramme on Tuesday against the previous closing of 4,825 rupees.
** Gold opens higher at 4,850 rupees but profit-taking trims early gains towards the close.
** Gold biscuit (116.50 gramme) closes 100 rupees higher at 56,500 rupees against previous closing of 56,400 rupees.
** Silver (.999) closes 95 rupees higher at 7,470 rupees per kg up against previous closing of 7,375 rupees on the back of upsurge in the world market as well as limited inflows.
"Gold opened higher today by 25 rupees at 4,850 rupees per 10 gramme on overnight gains in the world market but later on improved arrivals prompted profit-taking," said a dealer.
Gold was up by 35 rupees per 10 gramme on Monday.

Silver (.999) closed 95 rupees higher at 7,470 rupees per kg against the previous closing of 7,375 rupees on the back of speculative buying following a smart recovery in the world market. Fresh arrivals were low. Silver was down by 100 rupees per kg on Monday and by 170 rupees per kg during last week.
"Arrivals of imported silver in the Bombay market dropped today to 400/500 kg down against 1,400/1,500 rupees kg reported on Monday," one broker said. (Conversion $1=35.85 rupees)
